glossary.title: Baiting
glossary.def: you poke and wait for a reaction because you have nothing else. Everyone sees the hook. Nobody's biting.
glossary.line: Baiting: you poke and wait for a reaction because you have nothing else. Everyone sees the hook. Nobody's biting.

glossary.title: Deflection
glossary.def: 'just a joke', 'you're too sensitive'. You moved the target because you can't defend the shot. Weak dodge.
glossary.line: Deflection: 'just a joke', 'you're too sensitive'. You moved the target because you can't defend the shot. Weak dodge.

glossary.title: Dehumanizing
glossary.def: calling people animals or filth so harm feels okay. It says nothing about them and everything about you.
glossary.line: Dehumanizing: calling people animals or filth so harm feels okay. It says nothing about them and everything about you.

glossary.title: Pile-on
glossary.def: needing a crowd to win one argument. If your point was strong, you wouldn't need backup. Numbers aren't proof.
glossary.line: Pile-on: needing a crowd to win one argument. If your point was strong, you wouldn't need backup. Numbers aren't proof.

glossary.title: Slur swap
glossary.def: a stand-in word with the same meaning. Changing the spelling doesn't change the message. We all read it.
glossary.line: Slur swap: a stand-in word with the same meaning. Changing the spelling doesn't change the message. We all read it.

glossary.title: Slur evasion
glossary.def: dots, spaces, l33t to sneak it past a filter. The filter missed it. People didn't. Still a slur.
glossary.line: Slur evasion: dots, spaces, l33t to sneak it past a filter. The filter missed it. People didn't. Still a slur.

glossary.title: Code words
glossary.def: hate dressed up as inside jokes. Thinking nobody gets it is the funny part. People get it.
glossary.line: Code words: hate dressed up as inside jokes. Thinking nobody gets it is the funny part. People get it.

glossary.title: Slur
glossary.def: a word built to demean people for who they are. Not edgy, not brave, just lazy. Not here.
glossary.line: Slur: a word built to demean people for who they are. Not edgy, not brave, just lazy. Not here.

glossary.title: Gaslighting
glossary.def: insisting what everyone saw didn't happen. The chat log exists. Rewriting history only works on people who weren't there.
glossary.line: Gaslighting: insisting what everyone saw didn't happen. The chat log exists. Rewriting history only works on people who weren't there.

glossary.title: Whataboutism
glossary.def: can't defend your point, so you point at someone else. Everyone sees the dodge. Answer the question or admit you can't.
glossary.line: Whataboutism: can't defend your point, so you point at someone else. Everyone sees the dodge. Answer the question or admit you can't.

glossary.title: Concern trolling
glossary.def: fake worry to tear someone down. If you cared, you'd sound different. The mask is see-through.
glossary.line: Concern trolling: fake worry to tear someone down. If you cared, you'd sound different. The mask is see-through.

glossary.title: Strawman
glossary.def: you argue with a fake version of what they said because the real one beat you. Fight the real point or sit down.
glossary.line: Strawman: you argue with a fake version of what they said because the real one beat you. Fight the real point or sit down.

glossary.title: Goalpost moving
glossary.def: they met your demand, so you made a new one. That's not debate, that's running away slowly.
glossary.line: Goalpost moving: they met your demand, so you made a new one. That's not debate, that's running away slowly.

glossary.title: Sealioning
glossary.def: endless 'polite' questions you don't want answered, just to wear people out. Fake curiosity is still harassment.
glossary.line: Sealioning: endless 'polite' questions you don't want answered, just to wear people out. Fake curiosity is still harassment.

glossary.title: Tone policing
glossary.def: attacking how something was said because you can't touch what was said. The point still stands.
glossary.line: Tone policing: attacking how something was said because you can't touch what was said. The point still stands.

glossary.title: Ad hominem
glossary.def: attacking the person because the argument beat you. Insults are what's left when the logic runs out.
glossary.line: Ad hominem: attacking the person because the argument beat you. Insults are what's left when the logic runs out.

glossary.title: Gish gallop
glossary.def: twenty weak claims fired at once, hoping nobody checks. Quantity isn't quality. Pick your best one. Oh wait.
glossary.line: Gish gallop: twenty weak claims fired at once, hoping nobody checks. Quantity isn't quality. Pick your best one. Oh wait.

glossary.title: Just asking questions
glossary.def: smuggling a claim in as a 'question' so you can't be held to it. Say what you mean or own that you won't.
glossary.line: Just asking questions: smuggling a claim in as a 'question' so you can't be held to it. Say what you mean or own that you won't.

glossary.title: Victim blaming
glossary.def: making the hurt person the problem so the one who hurt them walks free. Obvious, and ugly.
glossary.line: Victim blaming: making the hurt person the problem so the one who hurt them walks free. Obvious, and ugly.

glossary.title: Othering
glossary.def: painting a group as 'not like us' so mistreating them feels fine. Old trick, same tired result.
glossary.line: Othering: painting a group as 'not like us' so mistreating them feels fine. Old trick, same tired result.

glossary.title: Scapegoating
glossary.def: blaming one group for everything because real answers are hard. Easy target, lazy thinking.
glossary.line: Scapegoating: blaming one group for everything because real answers are hard. Easy target, lazy thinking.

glossary.title: Stereotyping
glossary.def: judging millions of people by one cartoon. Says more about your imagination than about them.
glossary.line: Stereotyping: judging millions of people by one cartoon. Says more about your imagination than about them.

glossary.title: Dog piling
glossary.def: jumping on someone already outnumbered. Joining late to kick isn't bravery. It's following.
glossary.line: Dog piling: jumping on someone already outnumbered. Joining late to kick isn't bravery. It's following.

glossary.title: Trolling
glossary.def: saying things you don't believe to get a rise. If the reaction is your whole goal, you've got nothing. We see it.
glossary.line: Trolling: saying things you don't believe to get a rise. If the reaction is your whole goal, you've got nothing. We see it.

glossary.title: Flaming
glossary.def: all heat, no point. Shouting louder doesn't make you more right, just easier to ignore.
glossary.line: Flaming: all heat, no point. Shouting louder doesn't make you more right, just easier to ignore.

glossary.title: Doxxing threats
glossary.def: hinting you'll expose someone's private info to scare them. It's intimidation, it breaks the rules, and it's logged.
glossary.line: Doxxing threats: hinting you'll expose someone's private info to scare them. It's intimidation, it breaks the rules, and it's logged.

glossary.title: Outing
glossary.def: exposing someone's private identity to hurt them. Not truth-telling. Just cruelty with an excuse.
glossary.line: Outing: exposing someone's private identity to hurt them. Not truth-telling. Just cruelty with an excuse.

glossary.title: Misgendering on purpose
glossary.def: refusing someone's name for themselves to get a rise. Cheap, petty, and everyone notices.
glossary.line: Misgendering on purpose: refusing someone's name for themselves to get a rise. Cheap, petty, and everyone notices.

glossary.title: Deadnaming
glossary.def: using an old name on purpose to wound. Remembering it isn't the flex you think it is.
glossary.line: Deadnaming: using an old name on purpose to wound. Remembering it isn't the flex you think it is.

glossary.title: Mocking accents
glossary.def: when you can't beat what someone says, you mock how they say it. Tells us you lost the point.
glossary.line: Mocking accents: when you can't beat what someone says, you mock how they say it. Tells us you lost the point.

glossary.title: Love bombing
glossary.def: drowning someone in flattery to hook them fast. Too much, too soon is a tactic, not a feeling.
glossary.line: Love bombing: drowning someone in flattery to hook them fast. Too much, too soon is a tactic, not a feeling.

glossary.title: Negging
glossary.def: backhanded 'compliments' to knock someone down so they chase approval. Transparent and tired.
glossary.line: Negging: backhanded 'compliments' to knock someone down so they chase approval. Transparent and tired.

glossary.title: Guilt tripping
glossary.def: making someone feel bad so they do what you want. If you need guilt to win, you didn't have a reason.
glossary.line: Guilt tripping: making someone feel bad so they do what you want. If you need guilt to win, you didn't have a reason.

glossary.title: Silent treatment
glossary.def: freezing someone out to punish them. Ignoring isn't strength, it's control with the volume off.
glossary.line: Silent treatment: freezing someone out to punish them. Ignoring isn't strength, it's control with the volume off.

glossary.title: Rumor spreading
glossary.def: hurting someone where they can't answer back. If it were true, you'd say it to their face.
glossary.line: Rumor spreading: hurting someone where they can't answer back. If it were true, you'd say it to their face.

glossary.title: Impersonation
glossary.def: pretending to be someone to make them look bad. You had to borrow a name because yours has no weight.
glossary.line: Impersonation: pretending to be someone to make them look bad. You had to borrow a name because yours has no weight.

glossary.title: Spam flooding
glossary.def: burying the chat so nobody else can talk. Volume isn't a voice. It's just noise.
glossary.line: Spam flooding: burying the chat so nobody else can talk. Volume isn't a voice. It's just noise.

glossary.title: Brigading
glossary.def: calling in outsiders to swarm one room. Needing an army for one chat says it all.
glossary.line: Brigading: calling in outsiders to swarm one room. Needing an army for one chat says it all.

glossary.title: False equivalence
glossary.def: treating a paper cut and a broken leg as 'the same'. They aren't. Everyone can tell.
glossary.line: False equivalence: treating a paper cut and a broken leg as 'the same'. They aren't. Everyone can tell.

glossary.title: Appeal to tradition
glossary.def: 'it's always been this way'. So was a lot of bad stuff. Old isn't the same as right.
glossary.line: Appeal to tradition: 'it's always been this way'. So was a lot of bad stuff. Old isn't the same as right.

glossary.title: Minimizing
glossary.def: 'it's not a big deal' about harm you caused. You don't get to decide how much it hurt someone else.
glossary.line: Minimizing: 'it's not a big deal' about harm you caused. You don't get to decide how much it hurt someone else.

glossary.title: DARVO
glossary.def: deny, attack, then play the victim. Flipping the script so fast is the tell. We saw the order it happened in.
glossary.line: DARVO: deny, attack, then play the victim. Flipping the script so fast is the tell. We saw the order it happened in.

glossary.title: Triangulation
glossary.def: pulling a third person in to gang up or stir jealousy. Can't handle it one on one? Noted.
glossary.line: Triangulation: pulling a third person in to gang up or stir jealousy. Can't handle it one on one? Noted.

glossary.title: Intimidation
glossary.def: trying to scare people quiet because you can't win the argument. Fear isn't a point. It's a confession.
glossary.line: Intimidation: trying to scare people quiet because you can't win the argument. Fear isn't a point. It's a confession.

glossary.title: Threats
glossary.def: the last move of someone who's lost. Against Xat rules, logged, and it changes nothing here.
glossary.line: Threats: the last move of someone who's lost. Against Xat rules, logged, and it changes nothing here.

glossary.title: Sarcasm attack
glossary.def: mocking instead of answering so you never have to commit to a point. Smirking isn't an argument.
glossary.line: Sarcasm attack: mocking instead of answering so you never have to commit to a point. Smirking isn't an argument.

glossary.title: Emoji harassment
glossary.def: spamming clown or vomit emojis at someone. Tiny pictures, tiny argument. Still harassment.
glossary.line: Emoji harassment: spamming clown or vomit emojis at someone. Tiny pictures, tiny argument. Still harassment.

glossary.title: Projection
glossary.def: accusing others of exactly what you're doing. Funny how specific those accusations get.
glossary.line: Projection: accusing others of exactly what you're doing. Funny how specific those accusations get.

glossary.title: Changing the subject
glossary.def: losing on one topic, so you jump to another. Come back when you can finish the first one.
glossary.line: Changing the subject: losing on one topic, so you jump to another. Come back when you can finish the first one.

glossary.title: Floyding
glossary.def: turning a man's death into a meme to bait a reaction. Not edgy, just a cheap shock tactic from someone with nothing to say. Nobody's taking the bait.
glossary.line: Floyding: turning a man's death into a meme to bait a reaction. Not edgy, just a cheap shock tactic from someone with nothing to say. Nobody's taking the bait.

glossary.title: Fake neutrality
glossary.def: 'both sides are bad' to shield the side doing harm. Sitting on the fence still picks a side.
glossary.line: Fake neutrality: 'both sides are bad' to shield the side doing harm. Sitting on the fence still picks a side.
